races.name: Quinnbet.com Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rubellite
runners_data.note: Strong AW performer with three wins and eight places from 14 starts on Standard going, comfortably the best course-and-going profile in the race; tracks pace naturally and is well-suited to sitting just behind an uncontested front-runner at this 1m4f-plus trip, with a recent win at this distance on this surface boosting confidence at OR 62.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: In solid recent form (two wins in last six), but her record on Standard going is worrying — zero wins and zero places from three attempts — and though she is a natural hold-up horse, the controlled tempo here will force her to commit earlier than she ideally wants, reducing her chance of producing the late finish she needs.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Poor recent form figures (565373) and an almost non-existent record on Standard going (one run, unplaced) make her hard to trust even before accounting for the fact that this steady-tempo scenario will ask her to race more prominently than suits her; the 12-day turnaround is short and Alex Jary's 3lb claim offers limited compensation.

runners_data.name: Jujubella
runners_data.note: The highest-weighted runner in the field at 129lbs and rated OR 66, she has placed at this trip on Standard going and her hold-up style gives her some late-race appeal, though she has not won in recent starts and her heavy ground disaster (14th at Haydock) on soft underlines that Standard AW is the right environment; headgear (hood) noted.

runners_data.name: Sharona
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an immediate red flag for fitness and freshness, and her record on Standard going (0 wins, 0 places from one run) offers no encouragement; a genuine hold-up horse who will struggle to express her style in a slow-tempo race, and the tongue-plate addition cannot mask these significant concerns.

runners_data.name: Velvet Whisper
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — sole front-runner, rated OR 72, has won twice over this general trip and handles Standard going adequately (one place from three runs); her 18-day break looks fine and Cian Horgan's 5lb claim is a meaningful weight advantage; her recent form figures (886) since two wins reflect stiffer company rather than loss of ability, and uncontested lead is the key to her chance.

runners_data.name: Dior Noir
runners_data.note: 290 days off the track is a major concern and she is tagged as a horse who fades in the finish, a damaging trait in any scenario; her sole AW start produced a 2nd on Standard going which is mildly encouraging, but ring-rustiness combined with the stamina question at 1m4½f and the hold-up style makes her very hard to support on comeback.

races.paceDynamic: Velvet Whisper is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner fillies' handicap over 1m4½f on Newcastle's All-Weather, and with no rival likely to seriously contest her for the lead, she should settle into a controlled, unhurried gallop from the outset. The race is likely to be run at a steady-to-moderate tempo given the absence of any genuine pace pressure, which will compress the field through the middle stages and keep the race very much in Velvet Whisper's hands. Rubellite, rated highest among the prominent types, should track closely in second or third and is the horse most likely to benefit from sitting just off the easy pace. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Sharona, Recobella, and Princess Niyla are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions, meaning they are unlikely to secure the deep closing ground they need; in this controlled tempo they will be forced to make ground earlier than ideal, blunting their effectiveness. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles — Velvet Whisper dictating from the front and Rubellite tracking in her slipstream are the clear tactical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Velvet Whisper Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Whisper bowls along at a controlled tempo unchallenged, stealing an uncontested lead and quickening away in the straight.
scenarios.body: She controls every yard of the race, setting a pace that is just quick enough to string the field out without exhausting herself, then kicks clear before hold-up horses can close the gap. A steady gallop on Standard AW over this trip suits a front-runner who can dictate entirely on her own terms, and her rivals' inability to get their natural positions further aids her cause.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Whisper sets an honest enough gallop to tire in the final two furlongs, allowing the closest tracker to overhaul her late.
scenarios.body: Rubellite, with strong form at this track and trip on Standard going (14 qualifying runs, three wins), is perfectly positioned to inherit the lead if the front-runner fades, having tracked the pace throughout without expending excess energy. This is the most plausible upset scenario given Rubellite's course-and-going profile and the ability to switch off just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gatecrashes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and a truly slow gallop sets up a sprint finish that allows a hold-up runner to produce a late burst.
scenarios.body: Recobella carries the best recent winning form in the field (two wins in last six) and is the hold-up type most likely to find enough momentum if the race turns into a late dash, though her poor record on Standard going (0 wins, 0 places from 3 runs) is a significant concern. Princess Niyla and Sharona face similar style-fit and going-record obstacles, making this scenario a lower-probability proposition overall.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Favourite
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Whisper misses the break, suffers interference, or is ridden too aggressively early, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically messy pace scenario would scramble the shape entirely, potentially suiting whichever runner can best adapt mid-race, though with no dominant alternative pace-setter this remains a highly unlikely outcome. Jujubella, who has placed on Standard going and handles this trip, would be best equipped to capitalise on a chaotic race if her rivals are caught flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Velvet Whisper's early position is critical — if she misses the break or another runner pushes her into a faster gallop than intended, the entire race shape collapses and her winning chance reduces significantly.

Sharona ran only two days ago and connections should be monitored at the start for any signs of fatigue or reluctance; a lethargic early performance from her could further compress the midfield and leave hold-up horses with nowhere to go.

Dior Noir returns from 290 days off the track — watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages, and if she struggles to travel from the outset she could become a hazard to runners attempting to close from behind her.

Rubellite's draw and early positioning will be telling — if she slots in directly behind Velvet Whisper without expending energy, her Standard-going course form makes her the most dangerous horse in the race to the likely pace-setter in the final two furlongs.

Recobella's jockey Tom Kiely-Marshall should be watched for how aggressively he commits in the straight — if he is forced to produce his challenge a furlong earlier than ideal due to the compressed field, it will confirm the hold-up redistribution concern and likely rule her out of the finish.

races.name: Quinnbet Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Niffler
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins over 14f and 12f on Standard AW give her strong course-and-going form, and Sir Mark Prescott's operation is noted for placing horses precisely; her natural style is hold-up but she has been mapped to the front by default in the absence of any other pace, which is a role she will not relish — expect Poppy Scott (7lb claimer) to keep her settled and hope rivals are slow to challenge.

runners_data.name: Ada Rose
runners_data.note: Two from two over 12f-16f on Standard AW with Kevin Philippart De Foy's yard in fine recent form (4 from 20 in 14 days), and the 2d turnaround is worth noting — connections clearly feel she is spot-on; a natural hold-up performer with a strong similar-going record who should travel smoothly in this slowly-run contest and have the class to pull clear late.

runners_data.name: Star Of Markinch
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran whose last 15 runs on similar going have produced zero wins and zero places, with four consecutive fourths suggesting a horse that competes honestly but lacks the decisive finishing effort to get his head in front; Gary Rutherford's yard is winless in 14 days, and his true hold-up style being displaced into a midfield role by redistribution only adds to the burden of an already difficult profile.

runners_data.name: Lilykoy
runners_data.note: The 3lb claimer Alex Jary partners this three-year-old who has shown modest form in six career runs, with no wins and recent finishes of 4th, 3rd, and 8th suggesting a progressive but unproven stayer; naturally a hold-up horse whose position on the map has been pushed forward into midfield by the shape of the race, and the blinkers (hg:b) are worth noting as a potential headgear factor, though Dylan Cunha's 4 from 21 recent strike rate is modest.

races.paceDynamic: Niffler is the only horse mapped to the lead, though this is a redistribution — her true style is hold-up, but with no genuine front-runner in this four-runner field someone must set the tempo and she is the most likely candidate by default. At 2m½f on Standard AW at Newcastle, the pace is expected to be sustainable rather than scorching, with Niffler dictating a measured gallop that keeps the race honest without burning off the field. Ada Rose, Star Of Markinch, and Lilykoy are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the entire field is essentially waiting on each other, which could produce a slowly-run, bunched affair that turns into a sprint from the home straight. This shape strongly favours a horse with the ability to quicken from a prominent position late, and the lack of genuine pace means runners capable of travelling smoothly and producing a decisive late effort are best positioned — true hold-up specialists who need strong fractions to deliver their best may be compromised. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Star Of Markinch and Lilykoy are the most likely to find themselves pushed into midfield roles they are not naturally suited to, while Ada Rose, with the strongest recent form profile at the distance, is best placed to exploit a tactical, slowly-run contest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Tempo, Ada Rose Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Niffler sets a conservative, uncontested gallop and the race develops as a slow-burn test of quality finishing.
scenarios.body: Ada Rose, fresh from two wins at this sort of trip on Standard going, can travel comfortably just off the pace and produce a decisive effort once the race quickens in the final two furlongs; her class edge and strong similar-going record (six runs, one win, three places) make her the standout beneficiary of a steadily-run stamina test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Niffler Front, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Niffler, despite being a redistributed hold-up type, settles in front and finds the lack of pressure allows her to idle and then quicken when challenged.
scenarios.body: At 2m½f the extra trip may expose her hold-up tendencies, but her recent form shows two wins in her last three, and an uncontested lead at a conservative tempo could allow her to steal a march on her slower-reacting rivals; the 7lb claimer Poppy Scott keeping her balanced throughout is the key variable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is artificially slow enough that a sprint develops from three furlongs out and the rearmost runners get a brief flicker of opportunity.
scenarios.body: Star Of Markinch and Lilykoy would need the race to collapse into a flat-out dash from home, but both are redistributed hold-up types racing out of role in midfield, and Star Of Markinch's consistent string of fourths on Good ground does not inspire confidence on Standard AW; the scenario is possible but structurally weak given none of the supposed closers are genuine hold-up horses in true position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Total Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If no horse is willing to commit to the lead and the early pace collapses entirely, creating a falsely-run race that produces an unpredictable result.
scenarios.body: With all four runners being hold-up types by nature, a scenario where the field crawls and bunches into the home straight cannot be entirely dismissed, turning the race into a lottery; any horse with a sharp turn of foot in the final furlong would benefit, and Niffler's recent finishing effort must be considered if the race is run to suit her naturally.

watchPoints.text: Watch Ada Rose's early positioning — if Shane Gray gets her tracking Niffler comfortably within the first mile, her recent 16f and 12f Standard wins suggest she has the class to go clear once asked and could prove difficult to peg back.

Watch for a crawl in the early stages — with all four runners being natural hold-up horses, there is a genuine risk no one wants to commit, and if Niffler dwells or fails to stride on, the race could turn into a two-furlong dash that scrambles the form.

Star Of Markinch's record of zero wins or places in 15 runs on similar going is a significant red flag — watch for him to once again fill a minor position without ever threatening, particularly if the race lacks the strong gallop that suit his best efforts.

Lilykoy's headgear (blinkers) is worth monitoring at the start — if the headgear sharpens her early, she may occupy a more prominent position than her natural style suggests, but her raw form figures on Standard AW (8th) do not encourage confidence.

Watch Niffler's stride pattern once she clears the early stages — a horse fading in the finish (flagged) over this marathon 2m½f trip is a concern if any rival applies pressure from two furlongs out, and that late vulnerability may be the race's decisive tactical moment.

runners_data.name: Ormolulu
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who requires pace to run into; Conor Whiteley takes off 5lb but the 58-day absence and poor recent form (including a 0W2P strike rate at similar going) make her a speculative each-way hope at best.|

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a good record at 6f, including a win on good; Cam Hardie is a strong booking for this course, tp headgear retained, and the 25-day turnaround is brisk — gets in light and will look to track the leader throughout.|

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: Holds prominent tendencies in her natural style but is effectively squeezed out of that position by busier prominent traffic here, meaning she is likely to race further back than she'd prefer; Edward Bethell yard in cracking current form (3/27 over 14 days) and her sole 6f AW win was recorded on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Lady Kodiac
runners_data.note: Well-handicapped on a mark of 84 having placed twice at this course and distance, and James Tate's runners after a break (50 days) often arrive fit; Harry Vigors claims 5lb and she shapes as the most dangerous horse to Persian Spirit if the leader comes back to the field.|

runners_data.name: Persian Spirit
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with a clear lead and a winning course-and-distance record; 364-day layoff is the major concern, but Edward Bethell's yard is in hot form and Sam James is a reliable pilot — her ability to control the tempo is the dominant race-shaping factor.|

runners_data.name: Anaisa
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has run just 4 days ago for Tim Easterby, whose extremely high volume strike rate (10/83) suggests a yard firing; tongue-tie retained, but recent form is uninspiring and she needs significant pace to run into, which this race is unlikely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Dark Angel Light
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly who posted an impressive debut win over this exact course and trip; the follow-up was a well-beaten seventh on good ground, so the AW surface back here returns her to her winning environment — the absence (71 days) and small sample make her profile intriguing but uncertain.|

races.paceDynamic: Persian Spirit is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead role and no rival genuinely disputing for the front, she is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 6f Newcastle AW straight. Maldevious, Lady Kodiac, and Dark Angel Light are all prominent types who will push to race in the first half of the field, but they are passengers behind Persian Spirit rather than pace-makers against her — their presence applies pressure without creating a true sprint-from-the-front war. The hold-up pair Ormolulu and Anaisa will be doing their racing from off the pace and require the leaders to tie each other up, which is an unlikely outcome given Persian Spirit's uncontested status. This race shape strongly favours the front-to-prominent profile: a controlled solo lead on a flat, fair surface with no real pace pressure is the ideal canvas for a horse able to make all and quicken, and those racing close to Persian Spirit will be best placed to pounce if she fades. Note that Zarinca is a genuine prominent type who has been redistributed to midfield in the mapping because the prominent berths in this race are already overpopulated — Lady Kodiac and Maldevious are most likely to physically secure those positions ahead of her.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Persian Spirit Makes All
scenarios.trigger: If Persian Spirit dictates unchallenged from the front and sets a controlled, even gallop that plays to her stamina.
scenarios.body: Persian Spirit led wire-to-wire on her sole win at this course and distance, and with no horse willing to go with her, she can settle beautifully in front and use her recent layoff freshness to her advantage on return.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit The Line
scenarios.trigger: If Persian Spirit softens late in the final furlong and one of the tracking prominent horses runs past her.
scenarios.body: Lady Kodiac's solid record at this trip on AW with multiple placed efforts, and Maldevious having won over 6f on good, would both be poised just off the leader to capitalise if the pace tells on the long-time leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster push the early pace beyond Persian Spirit's comfort zone, creating a fast enough gallop to set up a late run.
scenarios.body: Ormolulu and Anaisa would need the race to be truly run to suit closers, which is structurally unlikely with a single uncontested leader — but if the track bias assists late runners, Ormolulu's 6f Newcastle form could make her dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Quickens Through
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Angel Light or Zarinca, both lightly raced, produce an unexpectedly sharp turn of foot from their respective positions.
scenarios.body: Dark Angel Light won impressively on debut over this trip and is an unknown quantity on a small form sample, while Zarinca — racing out of her natural prominent role — would need an unusually clean run from a compromised position to land this.

watchPoints.text: Persian Spirit's 364-day layoff is the single biggest vulnerability in the race — watch whether Sam James settles her immediately in front or if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness in the first furlong, as that will define the entire race shape.

Lady Kodiac is the most likely beneficiary if Persian Spirit fades; watch how quickly Harry Vigors positions her after the break — if she travels with ease in second or third, she becomes the primary danger in the straight.

Zarinca is racing out of her natural prominent role due to field composition; watch whether Jack Nicholls (3lb claim) attempts to push forward regardless, as any scrimmage for prominent positions early could cause interference and affect the race shape.

Dark Angel Light is lightly raced with an unknown ceiling — Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claim) is relatively inexperienced in competitive handicaps; monitor her starting price movement as market confidence or drift will be informative given the small form sample.

Anaisa ran just 4 days ago — watch her market and paddock demeanour; Tim Easterby's volume approach means quick returns are routine, but any sign of a non-trier run or market drift should be noted before assessing her hold-up chance.

runners_data.name: Showtown
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Kevin Ryan and Tom Eaves who has posted consistent placed efforts at 6f on good ground; six runs at the trip suggest he handles it well, and his OR 64 leaves room to improve if the pace burns ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Maximum Velocity
runners_data.note: Has shown ability with a second and third at 6f on good — his natural instinct is to come from the rear, but with Perineighs and Saxon Prince also needing that ground, getting a clean passage late will be harder than usual; style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Saxon Prince
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie) noted; won over 7f on Standard AW which is relevant, but 72 days off means he needs to strip fit, and his genuine hold-up style will be compromised here with the rear already crowded by redistributed runners.

runners_data.name: Dontwaste A Moment
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who won on Standard AW at 5f and wears a tongue-tie; he will be a willing participant in the early pace battle, but his tendency to be swallowed by more experienced rivals over 6f suggests he fires the race up more than he wins it.

runners_data.name: Storm Esme
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has strong turf form figures but her best came on good-to-soft at Newmarket; she goes prominently and her sole AW start produced a win at 5f, so the extra furlong on this surface is a mild stamina query — Sean Kirrane's claim is small compensation.

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: Highest-weighted at 135lbs alongside March Ahead and Riley Rocks; his recent form string of four consecutive placed or winning efforts on good ground is compelling, and he was beaten only a length or so last time — the concern is he has been running on good rather than Standard AW.

runners_data.name: Riley Rocks
runners_data.note: Shares top weight at OR 70 and has a pair of wins on Standard AW in his record, giving him the strongest course-surface credentials in the field; his form is inconsistent but the going suits, and Sam James provides a stable booking.

runners_data.name: March Ahead
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's colt was off 101 days and returns for a stamina test he may not relish if dragged into a war with Sea Her Excel and Dontwaste A Moment; David Nolan gives him every chance of controlling fractions, and his OR 70 win form is legitimate.

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Won two of her last five starts including over this course and distance, making her the most course-proven of the three pace horses; Elle-May Croot's 5lb claim helps at the weights but inexperience in a tactical battle against March Ahead is a question mark.

runners_data.name: Record Day
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a serious concern in a race guaranteed to test stamina; his form figures at 7f suggest he is better over longer trips, and this 6f strong-pace scenario looks against him.

runners_data.name: Comprador
runners_data.note: Has placed five times without winning and handles Standard AW going; Cam Hardie is a reliable booking around Newcastle and the horse shows enough consistency to be competitive if the pace produces a strong late stream.

runners_data.name: Believeinmenow
runners_data.note: Faye McManoman rides with a 7lb claim for Nigel Tinkler; the headgear change to a hood is noted and her two most recent efforts at 5f on Standard AW were solid placements — stepping up to 6f today should suit her prominent style.

runners_data.name: Celtic Arrow
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's filly has placed twice at 6f including on Standard AW and has been running consistently without winning; the shorter layoff of 19 days suggests she arrives cherry-ripe and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim makes the weights more attractive.

runners_data.name: Perineighs
runners_data.note: Spencer's gelding has placed at 5f twice on Standard AW but comes here as a true hold-up horse whose back-of-the-field preference will be squeezed out by the cluster of similarly patient runners; his 0-from-7 on similar going tempers confidence further.

races.paceDynamic: March Ahead, Sea Her Excel, and Dontwaste A Moment are all confirmed front-runners who will clash for position from the gates, guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop over this 6f Newcastle AW contest. With three genuine pace horses fighting for the lead from the outset, the early sectionals will be fierce, compressing the field and burning off those who try to maintain contact without natural early speed. This race shape squarely favours horses who can race prominently without expending maximum energy in the battle for the rail, or genuine late-closers who can absorb the pace and unleash a sustained finish — stamina and tactical efficiency will be at a premium. Perineighs, Maximum Velocity, and Saxon Prince are true hold-up operators who have been mapped to midfield only because the rear is oversubscribed; they are unlikely to secure their natural rearward position with this much pace in the race, which tempers their winning prospects in any shape that depends on them tracking the leaders from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace war between March Ahead, Sea Her Excel, and Dontwaste A Moment burns out the front-runners and a horse in close attendance survives the carnage.
scenarios.body: The three pace horses set a furious tempo that destroys them in the final furlong, and a horse sitting just off the boil in a prominent pitch — Showtown, Celtic Arrow, Believeinmenow, or Storm Esme — swoops to collect in the dying strides.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace horses breaks fastest, secures a clear lead unchallenged, and controls the tempo rather than being dragged into a duel.
scenarios.body: In this race shape the front-runner dictates a sustainable gallop after the others fail to match strides in the first two furlongs, building enough of a buffer to hold on; March Ahead has the class and a senior jockey in David Nolan to manage that scenario most convincingly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle proves even more gruelling than expected and genuine hold-up energy is preserved far enough back to unleash a telling late burst.
scenarios.body: Great Profit and Riley Rocks, who carry the highest official ratings in the field at OR 70, would be the primary beneficiaries of a properly run-ragged race; Comprador, who has repeatedly posted placed efforts staying on, could also figure if gap-finding permits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Tactics Nullified
scenarios.trigger: If one pace horse is withdrawn or badly checked early and the race unexpectedly settles into a muddling, falsely run contest.
scenarios.body: A steadier gallop compacts the field and reduces the stamina test, negating the hold-up runners entirely and rewarding whichever prominent type conserves energy best; Celtic Arrow, with two recent placed efforts on similar surfaces, and Believeinmenow with her course experience, would be best placed.

watchPoints.text: March Ahead, Sea Her Excel, and Dontwaste A Moment will all break hard for the front — watch the first two furlongs for a pace-blow that could burn out all three, leaving the race to prominent stalkers Showtown or Celtic Arrow.

Riley Rocks holds the joint-top OR alongside Great Profit and March Ahead and has demonstrated wins on Standard AW; if he gets a trouble-free run from midfield off a hot pace, he is the single most dangerous horse in the race.

Record Day is flagged as fading in the finish — in a race with a guaranteed strong gallop, any punter's money on him should note this stamina deficiency is likely to be exposed emphatically over the final furlong.

Maximum Velocity, Perineighs, and Saxon Prince all want to race from the rear but the rear is genuinely oversubscribed — watch for scrimmaging and blocked exits in the straight as they all seek the same late run.

Sea Her Excel is the only front-runner with a proven winning record over this exact course and distance; if she breaks fastest and David Nolan on March Ahead has to chase, it is Sea Her Excel who controls the fractions rather than March Ahead.

runners_data.name: Yaajooz
runners_data.note: Hasn't won in 15 attempts, last ran 93 days ago and his sim-going record reads 0W1P from 3 runs — in his heart a hold-up horse, though the glut of closers in this field means he will track closer to midfield than his natural position; hard to make a case at OR=68 given the form string 27-890.|

runners_data.name: Highfield Viking
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who travels well off a pace, though his entire recent history was run on Good ground and he has only one placing from 15 runs in similar conditions — the step to Standard AW is the key question for Dougie Costello to answer.|

runners_data.name: Enpassant
runners_data.note: Two wins from 13 runs in Standard going and four places makes him statistically the most course-and-conditions-proven horse in the race; his front-foot racing style suits a Spartan Fighter-led tempo perfectly, and Christian Howarth's 3lb claim offsets any fitness concern after 71 days off.|

runners_data.name: Jamaican Storm
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course, distance and going last time before a modest outing at Goodwood; his true style is hold-up but the race shape forces him forward of his natural position, so David Nolan will need to be pragmatic — the sim-going record of 2W6P from 10 runs is the strongest in the field and keeps him relevant.|

runners_data.name: Wish This
runners_data.note: Landed his sole AW win over this trip in Standard conditions but has finished 8th, 9th, and 6th in his last three — a natural hold-up type squeezed into a midfield slot by the field's make-up, and the headgear note (blinkers) suggests connections are trying to sharpen him up; Tom Eaves will need plenty of luck in running.|

runners_data.name: Spartan Fighter
runners_data.note: The race's only front-runner, with a visored veteran who has won four times and placed eight times from 14 runs in Standard going — the 183-day layoff is the single biggest concern, but Antony Brittain is adept at producing horses fresh and the tactical advantage of leading is substantial here.|

runners_data.name: Sunriseontheboyne
runners_data.note: Returned a winner over 8f in Standard last time but this drop to 7f and a turnaround of just three days is a notable freshness flag; OR=70 is top-weight territory and the 5lb claim of Harry Vigors theoretically offsets some of that, but the hold-up style is poorly suited to the likely pace of this race.|

runners_data.name: Criminal Shore
runners_data.note: Joint-top-rated at OR=70 and also raced just three days ago — back-to-back outings in a short window is a concern — the visor is retained from recent runs and O'Meara's 7/50 in 14 days shows the yard is in good form, but a hold-up style in a steady-pace race limits Conor Whiteley's options.|

runners_data.name: Feel The Need
runners_data.note: Form string 0-2006 is bleak and the sim-going record of 0W1P from 3 runs offers little comfort; a genuine hold-up type who needs a strong pace that this race is highly unlikely to provide, and OR=70 feels flattering given recent evidence.|

races.paceDynamic: Spartan Fighter is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control this race from the front at a sustainable, unhurried gallop over Newcastle's straight seven furlongs. The pace is unlikely to be truly honest — one horse setting its own tempo without pressure typically produces a falsely-run contest where the front compresses the field and stamina tests are reduced. With Highfield Viking and Enpassant the most natural prominent racers to push forward and fill the early positions behind the leader, the middle and late portions of the race will be dictated by who can make their move around the two-furlong pole. This race shape strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles who can travel in a good position and kick, rather than true hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close — the field carries more hold-up types than the map can place, with Yaajooz, Jamaican Storm, and Wish This all redistributed rearward, and of those three, Jamaican Storm (most recent win over this course and distance in Standard) is best equipped to pivot from genuine hold-up to a midfield-tracking role if the pace stays moderate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spartan Fighter Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Spartan Fighter leads unbothered and sets a measured, controlled fractions that reward those racing prominently.
scenarios.body: Spartan Fighter dictates from the front at a fair but undemanding pace, with Highfield Viking and Enpassant tracking in his wake and the hold-up horses unable to close the gap through the final two furlongs on a flat, galloping track. Prominent types who can travel smoothly and kick off the front edge are the primary beneficiaries, with the front-runner himself a live threat if the weight and long layoff (183 days) haven't blunted his sharpness.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Highfield Viking or Enpassant track Spartan Fighter closely and produce a stronger finishing effort over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A steady early pace sees the race come to a sprint from two furlongs out, with the prominent pair well-placed to challenge and pass a tiring front-runner whose 183-day absence may tell late. Enpassant's two wins at Newcastle in Standard conditions on this trip make him the standout beneficiary of this shape, and Highfield Viking's consistent prominent racing gives him a secondary claim.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected early and the closers get a genuine gallop to aim at through the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Jamaican Storm, who won over this course and distance last time in Standard conditions, would be best positioned of the redistributed hold-up horses to find a gap and close if the pace genuinely develops, though all three true hold-up types are mapped out of their natural position. Sunriseontheboyne or Criminal Shore, both rated OR=70 and each with a recent win on the board, could also pick up the pieces if the front end fades.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Top-Rated Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Sunriseontheboyne or Criminal Shore, the two joint-highest-rated runners at OR=70, outclass the field in the final furlong despite the unfavourable pace shape.
scenarios.body: Both ran just three days ago which is a significant flag, but top-rated horses occasionally overcome an unfavourable setup through sheer class; Criminal Shore's visor could sharpen focus if the gaps open, while Sunriseontheboyne's recent win over 8f in Standard suggests he may be stretching in stamina terms dropping to 7f here. This scenario requires the pace to be more honest than the setup implies and remains a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Spartan Fighter's 183-day layoff is the pivotal unknown — if Cam Hardie can get him bowling along comfortably in the early stages, the uncontested lead makes him the horse to beat, but any sign of ring-rustiness in the first furlong could let Highfield Viking or Enpassant steal a march.

Sunriseontheboyne and Criminal Shore both ran just three days ago — watch their pre-race demeanour and early market movement; back-to-back quick turnarounds for OR=70-rated hold-up horses in a race that shapes up to suit front-runners is a compound disadvantage.

Enpassant's 71-day absence could mean he comes here needing the run, but his two previous wins at Newcastle in Standard going are directly relevant — monitor whether Scott Dixon has sent him ready or just for fitness.

With Yaajooz, Jamaican Storm, and Wish This all genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield positions by the race shape, the closing quarter-mile could become congested if any of them commit to the same gap — David Nolan on Jamaican Storm is the most experienced jockey of the three and best placed to exploit any opening.

races.name: Free Tips On Attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Red Mirage
runners_data.note: A front-to-prominent runner for John & Sean Quinn; Harry Vigors (5) claims useful weight, and the horse has course experience on Standard AW but placed form here is limited at 0 wins from 2 relevant starts — held up only by consistency rather than class.

runners_data.name: War Howl
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners this Ben Haslam hold-up performer who carries a worrying late-fade flag and a string of double-figure finishes on Good, though this Standard AW surface is a different test; 21 days between runs is fine but the form figures of 000097 demand significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Blazing Son
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's eight-year-old races prominently and has solid course familiarity on Standard AW — one win and five placings from 11 starts at Newcastle AW is the strongest course record in this field; 44 days off the track is within normal bounds for this type.

runners_data.name: Coramento
runners_data.note: Ray Craggs's five-year-old is prominently raced and has an outstanding surface-specific record of four wins from 13 runs on Standard going, including a course win over 7f; Jack Nicholls's 3lb claim adds appeal and the horse has twice won over longer trips here, suggesting he will stay well.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Strong course and distance form for Katie Scott, but this is a genuine hold-up horse wearing a visor whose natural position at the rear is compromised by redistribution into midfield — only 11 days since last run is worth monitoring as a possible quick-turnaround fitness angle.

runners_data.name: Finn Ironside
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's five-year-old is fitted with a tongue-tie and is at heart a come-from-behind type whose best results on Standard AW came when given time to wind up late; placed in midfield due to field congestion at the rear, which reduces the likelihood of him producing his natural finish pattern.

runners_data.name: Anthropologist
runners_data.note: The joint top-weight at OR 70 for Michael Herrington, this hold-up horse has a strong AW profile on Standard — one win and five places from 13 starts — and wears a hood (hg:p) which has featured in recent runs; Sam James is a quality pilot and 44 days off the track is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Benacre
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's stable in excellent form (T14: 5/39) and Benacre is the confirmed pace-setter; despite consistent recent form of 550545, this horse has only a limited winning record and a STYLE_FIT flag indicates it may not be fully exploiting its front-running advantage here — worth watching whether Jonny Peate actually commits to the lead from stall draw.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's five-year-old has a genuine win from 8f on Good (AW) and ran well to third over 7f on similar; Jack Garritty rides a horse that naturally sits off the pace and times a late run — the flat nature of the track at Newcastle suits a clean closing move if any pace collapse occurs in the final furlong.

races.paceDynamic: Benacre is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be afforded a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front on this flat Newcastle AW 7f. Red Mirage and Coramento will press forward into prominent positions behind Benacre, creating a structured, single-file pace scenario without any early burning of fuel by the leader. Anthropologist, Jesmond Dawn, and War Howl will attempt to sit off the pace and deliver late runs, but on a flat track at a sustainable tempo, those hold-up types will need the front-runners to tie themselves up, which looks unlikely here. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track Benacre closely and sustain through the final furlong, rather than closers who depend on a strongly-run race creating a gap. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Gressington and Finn Ironside are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots, meaning their natural late-race role is compromised and they are unlikely to get ideal cover or timing in this scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Benacre Controls, Held On
scenarios.trigger: If Benacre takes the lead uncontested and is allowed to dictate a measured, sustainable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Benacre sets a comfortable gallop with Red Mirage and Coramento in pursuit, and the pace never quickens enough to play into the hands of the hold-up horses; the race is decided between the prominent runners at the furlong pole. Coramento, with strong course form on Standard AW ground and an OR of 64, is well placed to challenge as the leader hits the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collide
scenarios.trigger: If Red Mirage and Coramento push the pace early, applying pressure to Benacre and lifting the tempo above comfortable.
scenarios.body: Benacre's advantage is eroded if two prominent rivals crowd him into racing faster than ideal, and the increased tempo opens a window for the best-quality hold-up horse to close ground late. Anthropologist, the highest-rated hold-up type at OR 70 with solid STA course form, is the most credible beneficiary if the pace is genuinely honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Benacre's stamina reserves are depleted after sustaining the gallop alone and the race collapses inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Jesmond Dawn, a winner over shorter on Good ground and with strong form near the pace, could scythe past a tiring front rank if the race unravels late; War Howl's pattern of fading late is a concern but David Nolan could engineer a position closer to the pace than usual on a flat track. This scenario requires a faster-than-expected early pace and relies on closers getting a clean run, both of which are against the grain of the dominant shape here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments and both the front group and closers misjudge, leaving a midfield horse to thread through for an unexpected win.
scenarios.body: Gressington and Finn Ironside are genuine hold-up horses positioned in midfield due to redistribution, meaning they are racing out of their natural role and timing their run from an unfamiliar position; their chance here is consequently discounted. Blazing Son is the more natural midfield-to-prominent runner who could benefit from a muddled finish, having placed here on Standard AW ground previously.

watchPoints.text: Coramento's four wins on Standard going combined with a course win over 7f and a 3lb claim for Jack Nicholls makes this horse the single biggest danger if it secures a prominent position and the pace is sustainable — watch whether it gets clear daylight entering the straight.

Benacre's STYLE_FIT tag means Jonny Peate's commitment to the front is not guaranteed; if Benacre fails to stride on cleanly from the gates and allows Red Mirage or Coramento to usurp the lead, the pace dynamic shifts materially.

Gressington's 11-day turnaround is the shortest gap in this field — watch for any signs of a quick-return fitness issue on track, particularly as it is already racing out of its natural hold-up role due to redistribution.

War Howl's consistent late-fade pattern across multiple recent Good-ground starts is a notable flag; if David Nolan attempts to ride it more prominently than usual to counteract this, it could inject unexpected pace pressure into the early stages and alter the race shape.

Anthropologist at OR 70 is the class benchmark among the hold-up horses — if Benacre sets an easy pace and the prominent runners fail to kick decisively, Sam James will have Anthropologist poised to deliver the most potent single late challenge in the field.

races.name: Attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a clean recent record of placed efforts over 8-9f on good and soft, gives Jack Nicholls a straightforward brief; 15 days between runs is ideal, no going concern on standard, and the step up in trip beyond her last few 8f runs may suit this 7-year-old mare well.

runners_data.name: Ey Up He's A Star
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground on his most recent start — that form is directly relevant — but he is a natural front-end or prominent horse whose true style cannot be expressed here with Relevant Range dominating; effective chance relies on a scenario where he can travel closer than his mapped position implies.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Five consecutive placed efforts at 7-8f, four of them over this exact trip, and T14 form of 2/14 suggests trainer is placing him with purpose; only 3 days between runs which is worth noting, and although he instinctively wants to race prominently, the unchallenged leader makes that difficult — his effectiveness depends on how the race is run rather than his own preference.

runners_data.name: Age Of Time
runners_data.note: Returns after 82 days off, which is a significant query, and though his sim-going record (11/15) is excellent for this track type, he is a natural hold-up horse being asked to race off a slow single-leader pace; Steph Hollinshead T14 rate of 1/5 is light but the long absence is the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Pete
runners_data.note: No wins in recent form and no placed efforts on anything resembling this surface or going (0W0P in sim-going), headgear noted as t (tongue tie), and the drop from 10f in his last two runs to 8f is interesting but form figures of 009628 don't encourage; Alex Jary (3) rides.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground (1 in recent form) and has course form to draw on, so the trip and surface are not concerns; Tom Eaves takes the ride, and while his natural hold-up style is out of sync with a slow-leader scenario, a genuinely run race suits him more than most in this field.

runners_data.name: Chuzzlewit
runners_data.note: The most interesting profile here — three placed efforts in his last five at this trip on this surface, including consecutive seconds on standard at Newcastle, making him the standout course-and-distance form candidate; Cam Hardie rides for a stable with recent course activity, and he appears a genuine closer whose profile suits the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Look Back Smiling
runners_data.note: Headgear noted as b (blinkers), and the trainer T14 rate of 0/8 is uninspiring; form string of -04376 shows a return to action recently with modest efforts, the 10f start two runs ago suggests connections are searching for his best trip, and the hold-up style is genuine but needs a stronger pace than Relevant Range alone is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Relevant Range
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and fulcrum of the whole race — won over 8f on good going two runs back and has placed course form on standard; Elle-May Croot (5) holds the tactical advantage of getting a clean lead, but Ivan Furtado's T14 figure of 0/17 is the softening factor, and her [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that in shape-specific terms her chance varies sharply by how much she can control the tempo.

races.paceDynamic: Relevant Range is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine and, with no genuine rival prepared to dispute the lead, she is set to dictate a controlled, unchallenged gallop around the Newcastle AW mile. The pace she sets will be honest but manageable — a lone leader on standard ground over a flat mile rarely burns herself out — which historically favours those who can travel in behind and produce a clean sustained finish. Every other runner in the field carries a hold-up profile, meaning the race becomes a question of who can pick off Relevant Range late, but the redistribution of Ey Up He's A Star, Starliner, Age Of Time, Whiskey Pete, Daring Leader and others into midfield is positional fiction — none of them are true closers hunting a fast pace, and a slow single-file procession may actually deny them the sustained gallop they need to peel and finish. The dominant tactical verdict is clear: a single front-runner controlling a fair but uncontested pace on flat standard ground is a shape that suits a patient hold-up horse with a strong finishing kick — provided that horse is a genuine stayer-on rather than one of the displaced prominent types mapped artificially to the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Relevant Range Leads Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Relevant Range secures the front and controls tempo without a serious challenger through the middle mile.
scenarios.body: Relevant Range dictates every yard at a fair but unforced gallop, arriving at the straight with petrol in the tank; the rest are forced to pass her rather than run onto a strong pace, suiting her finishing reserves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough that true hold-up runners can close the gap in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Second Fiddle and Chuzzlewit, as legitimate hold-up types with strong recent form on comparable surfaces, find the tempo sufficient to mount a sustained challenge; Chuzzlewit's course-consistent placed form on this track at this distance is directly relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grab Places
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed midfield horses push forward from the break, disrupting the single-leader dynamic and creating a more contested early gallop.
scenarios.body: A faster early tempo tests Relevant Range's stamina and opens a contested race where front-to-midfield runners like Ey Up He's A Star and Daring Leader, who have won at this trip, can benefit from a more pressured shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that all runners bunch and the race becomes a two-furlong dash, negating hold-up form entirely.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling tempo benefits those who can quicken from a close-up position; Starliner's consistent placed form and Ey Up He's A Star's recent win suggest enough tactical speed to profit if the final furlong becomes a flat sprint.

watchPoints.text: Relevant Range sets the entire pace alone — if she quickens approaching the straight and kicks clear before closers can respond, she may prove very difficult to catch in a race with no pressure from the front.
Chuzzlewit has placed three times in five runs at Newcastle over this trip on standard ground — watch for him to be produced late by Cam Hardie as the most course-fit hold-up horse in the field.

Ey Up He's A Star and Daring Leader are both natural prominent types mapped to midfield; if either breaks sharply and pushes forward early, the pace dynamic changes materially and the scenario probabilities shift with it.

Age Of Time returns after 82 days off — watch the market and his early behaviour in the stalls; a freshened horse with strong sim-going figures can be dangerous returning from a break but needs to handle the layoff.

Whiskey Pete has zero placed efforts in comparable going conditions and drops from 10f; if the pace is slow, his finishing kick is unlikely to be sufficient, but in any scenario where the field strings out he becomes a monitoring horse for position-based overlay.
